findings.evidence: Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/Matrix/PosDef.lean:148-150 gives `PosSemidef (∑ i ∈ s, x i)` (matrix-valued). TauCeti/Analysis/PositiveDefinite/Basic.lean:279-285 and TauCeti/Analysis/PositiveDefinite/SemigroupGroup/Basic.lean:352-358 each contain the identical `have h := Matrix.posSemidef_sum s ...` / `have heq : (∑ i ∈ s, fun a b => ...) = fun a b => ∑ i ∈ s, ...` / `exact heq ▸ h` block, whereas Basic.lean:288-291 and SemigroupGroup/Basic.lean:362-366 route straight through `posSemidef_schur_finset_prod`. The deleted TauCeti/Analysis/PositiveDefinite/Kernel/Closure.lean provided `isPositiveDefiniteKernel_sum` in applied form.
findings.fix: Add `theorem posSemidef_schur_finset_sum {ι : Type w} {s : Finset ι} {K : ι → α → α → 𝕜} (hK : ∀ i ∈ s, Matrix.PosSemidef (K i)) : Matrix.PosSemidef (fun a b => ∑ i ∈ s, K i a b)` next to the product form (same `heq ▸ h` proof against `Matrix.posSemidef_sum`), list it in the module docstring, and rewrite `IsPositiveDefinite.sum` and `IsSemigroupGroupPD.sum` as one-liners like their `prod` counterparts.
findings.issue: `posSemidef_schur_finset_prod` supplies the function-applied finite product, but the file exposes no function-applied finite sum. Mathlib's `Matrix.posSemidef_sum` concludes about the matrix-valued `∑ i ∈ s, x i`, not `fun a b => ∑ i ∈ s, K i a b`, so the deleted `isPositiveDefiniteKernel_sum` has no replacement and both in-repo sum consumers re-derive the same transport.

summary: The migration is clean: no compatibility alias survives, helpers stay private, and every new public declaration has a consumer. One accepted API gap remains unimplemented — the replacement file has the applied-form finite Schur product but no applied-form finite sum, so both consumers open-code the transport from Mathlib's matrix-valued `posSemidef_sum`.
